title: Tarot of Intervals
source: wands.pdf as delivered. cards/: the composed card fronts rendered from the PDF pages at 300 dpi; art/: the embedded illustrations extracted unmodified (1024 x 1536).
note: Titles, keywords, symbolism, Opening/Snag, questions and Goetic associations as the illustrator's key gives them (wands-reading-key.pdf). The illustrator kept the draft's Seven, Page and Knight and re-titled the other eleven; the Goetic associations are its adaptations of the draft.

cards.title: The Kindled Rod
cards.symbolism: A singer holds a rod whose bud is beginning to open. The song and the bud answer one another without deciding which began first. There is enough energy to start; its eventual form remains to be discovered.
cards.upright: An impulse worth exploring; creative energy; a beginning made tangible.
cards.reversed: Waiting for a complete explanation before starting; ignition without something that can sustain it.
cards.question: What small act would give this impulse a form?
cards.name: Ace of Wands

cards.title: The Turning Measure
cards.symbolism: Two rods turn around a shared pivot while two routes remain open. The traveler tests the relation between intention and reach. Choosing a direction makes a journey possible without proving the other route was mistaken.
cards.upright: Planning; a choice tested against conditions; room to change direction.
cards.reversed: Comparing indefinitely; mistaking a plan for a journey; narrowing the choice too soon.
cards.question: What would you need to learn before committing to one route?
cards.name: Two of Wands

cards.title: The Joined Venture
cards.symbolism: Three rods meet above a shared basin. Each participant contributes a different angle, and the water receives the disturbance. A venture has begun; what happens next depends partly on how the participants answer one another.
cards.upright: An undertaking launched; complementary abilities; work that reaches beyond one person.
cards.reversed: Parallel intentions mistaken for agreement; waiting for responses that were never requested.
cards.question: What response would tell you that this venture is becoming shared?
cards.name: Three of Wands

cards.title: The Held Gathering
cards.symbolism: Four people hold one canopy over an open place. Its intricate fabric is supported at four points, and a small red binding joins its upper seam. The shelter is real, though someone must continue to maintain it.
cards.upright: A gathering sustained; welcome; a structure adequate to celebration and rest.
cards.reversed: Maintenance falling to too few people; a celebration with no room for those who sustain it.
cards.question: Who helps this place remain welcoming, and when do they get to rest?
cards.name: Four of Wands

cards.title: The Trial of Five
cards.symbolism: Five rods pull through separate clamps on one curved frame. Their differing directions create the trial. The small red adjustment changes one relation without settling all the others; skill grows through attending to the result.
cards.upright: Productive disagreement; practice; learning what changes under pressure.
cards.reversed: Competition without a shared task; repeating the trial without noticing what it teaches.
cards.question: What would make this friction instructive?
cards.name: Five of Wands

cards.title: The Shared Acclaim
cards.symbolism: Three colleagues hold six rods, joined by a red thread. Recognition reaches a person through a network of contributions. The achievement can be deserved, and acknowledging its support need not diminish it.
cards.upright: Success acknowledged; confidence supported by experience; credit shared without being erased.
cards.reversed: Depending on applause for direction; overlooking a contribution; difficulty accepting earned recognition.
cards.question: What deserves recognition here, and who helped make it possible?
cards.name: Six of Wands

cards.title: The Held Height
cards.symbolism: One crosswise rod meets six approaches. The flame gives resolve a visible voice, while the long tail carries the duration of commitment. The ground may deserve defending even if an expected reward never arrives.
cards.upright: Courage under pressure; a boundary held with purpose; speaking for something worth protecting.
cards.reversed: Defending a position after its purpose has changed; spending strength that needs replenishment.
cards.question: What is worth protecting here, and what would let you stand down?
cards.name: Seven of Wands

cards.title: The Dispatch
cards.symbolism: Eight rods cross the open space between two messengers. One is marked in red, but its importance does not guarantee that it will be understood. Sending and receiving belong to the same exchange, at different moments.
cards.upright: Swift communication; coordinated movement; an opening in which to act.
cards.reversed: Too many messages at once; speed outrunning understanding; arrival mistaken for receipt.
cards.question: What would show that this has been received?
cards.name: Eight of Wands

cards.title: The Patient Watch
cards.symbolism: Eight rods mark the wheel around a seated watcher; the ninth supports the hands at rest. One red point holds attention among many observations. Endurance includes waiting, and the watch can be passed to another person.
cards.upright: Patient attention; experience brought to bear; conserving strength while remaining present.
cards.reversed: Staying on watch without relief; vigilance that no longer distinguishes change from repetition.
cards.question: What needs your attention now, and what would make relief possible?
cards.name: Nine of Wands

cards.title: The Load Distributed
cards.symbolism: Ten rods stand in two racks while two helpers adjust a carrying strap. The work is substantial and the carriers have limits. Sharing the load changes its arrangement; it does not make the work disappear.
cards.upright: Responsibility made manageable; practical help; finishing through distribution and care.
cards.reversed: Accepting more than can be carried; sharing the appearance of work while leaving its weight unchanged.
cards.question: What can be handed over, set down, or finished?
cards.name: Ten of Wands

cards.title: The Reader of Ashes
cards.symbolism: The apprentice listens to the birds and studies the ash. A red mark gives attention somewhere to begin. Understanding may arrive in a fleeting form; the task is to notice it without turning the first impression into the whole answer.
cards.upright: Curiosity; receptive intelligence; a message that invites further inquiry.
cards.reversed: Rushing to interpret; collecting signals without testing a reading; a useful clue overlooked.
cards.question: What did you notice, and what would help you understand it?
cards.name: Page of Wands

cards.title: The Ridden Discord
cards.symbolism: The rider raises a wooden staff as the wolf gathers momentum. A red line connects that movement to an open circle behind it. Energy can carry an intention farther than expected; a route of return remains worth considering.
cards.upright: Courageous movement; enthusiasm with direction; a venture advanced through commitment.
cards.reversed: Impatience; momentum outrunning preparation; difficulty changing course once moving.
cards.question: How can this energy move freely and still find a way back?
cards.name: Knight of Wands

cards.title: The Open Court
cards.symbolism: The queen stands beside an unoccupied seat and welcomes a visitor. A bud opens on the staff. Warmth has a practical form: there is room to approach, room to speak, and room to decide what can be offered.
cards.upright: Confident welcome; creative generosity; warmth that can sustain a boundary.
cards.reversed: Offering more than can be sustained; warmth made conditional on agreement; retreating from useful exchange.
cards.question: What can you welcome without promising more than you can give?
cards.name: Queen of Wands

cards.title: The Answering Standard
cards.symbolism: The king holds a standard while listening to a colleague. A red repair remains visible in its fabric. Direction can be given without ending the conversation, and a visible revision need not undo the standing to act.
cards.upright: Leadership open to response; a direction people can work with; responsibility accepted.
cards.reversed: Treating a first vision as final; listening without allowing an answer to matter; authority avoiding its own repairs.
cards.question: What response could change the direction you are asking others to follow?
cards.name: King of Wands

reading: Wands give intention a form: a rod can kindle, measure, connect, support, contest or carry. An action may accomplish its purpose while remaining dependent on circumstances, other people and finite capacity. Red marks an intervention; its consequences remain open.
